text:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Significant latency and 5xx spike on /v1/generate (us-west-2). 95p latency jumped from 120ms -> 2.1s in the last 3m. Runtime metrics show KV cache entries skyrocketing and continuous-batching queue depth climbing. Paging @sre-oncall. Root ts 1845023456
Sam: On it. Noticed memory pressure on runtime pods — kvcache entries ~24M for one shard, evictions spiking. Suspect continuous-batching + high concurrency + disabled jitter causing synchronized cache population.
Sam: Immediate mitigation plan: 1) cap concurrency for public tier to 100 2) reduce microbatch max to 2 3) re-enable microbatch jitter 30-70ms 4) increase kvcache eviction aggressiveness
Sam: Running throttles now: `redwoodctl runtime set --region us-west-2 --concurrency-limit public=100` -> started
Luca: I’m on the kvcache config. Applying eviction limit and TTL: `redwoodctl runtime patch --kvcache.max_entries=150000 --kvcache.default_ttl=30s --kvcache.eviction_policy=lru`
Jordan: I pushed a dynamic flag to re-enable jitter: `redwoodctl feature-flags set continuous_batch_jitter_ms=50` and set microbatch max to 2: `redwoodctl runtime set --microbatch.max_size=2`
eng-deploy-bot: Deploy started for runtime-config-update-1845023456 — 6 pods rolling.
Sam: Observability: queue depth is decreasing, tail latency trending down from 2.1s -> 480ms in last 90s. Error rate (5xx) falling from 3.1% -> 0.6%.
Priya: Customer impact check: AcmePayments (dedicated customer) reported increased p99 latency and a few >=500s for webhook calls. Engineering support has opened a ticket and applied routing to fallback model variant (no prefix cache) for their requests.
Sam: Hotfix note for oncall: if latency climbs again, disable continuous-batching on the runtime tier: `redwoodctl runtime toggle --continuous-batching=false` and route traffic to non-cached variant. This avoids kvcache thundering.
Luca: Logs from a crashed shard: ```
[2026-03-15T14:12:21Z] kvcache: entries=24231456, mem=87%, evictions/sec=1200
[2026-03-15T14:12:22Z] runtime: microbatch_wait=0ms, queued=420, inflight=192
[2026-03-15T14:12:23Z] oom_killer: runtime/shard-3 killed process 3241
```
Sam: Reconcile: main trigger looks like a pattern where many concurrent requests build identical prefixes (small temperature / deterministic prompts), no jitter -> same cache addresses populated simultaneously, kvcache growth + mem pressure -> evictions -> more cold misses -> cascades.
Priya: Handoff to me for the next 2 hours. Current status: stabilized, throttles applied, eviction policy tightened, jitter re-enabled. AcmePayments on fallback. Create SEV-2 incident and attach timeline.
Priya: Action items for follow-up: - run synthesis test with high concurrency + identical prefix prompts to reproduce - consider defaulting jitter > 30ms in runtime by default - add kvcache soft cap metric alert at 5M entries - write a rollback playbook for continuous-batching
Jordan: I’m capturing commands + dashboards in the incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1845023456
Sam: Closing notes before handoff: applied throttles at 14:13:10Z, kvcache params patched at 14:14:05Z, jitter flag at 14:14:40Z, p95 returned under 300ms at 14:16:20Z. Will follow-up on RCA later.
Priya: Thanks — I’ll take it and keep paging if we see regression. Marking thread for postmortem and linking to kvcache regression experiments.
eng-deploy-bot: Deploy runtime-config-update-1845023456 succeeded in 6/6 pods.
Priya: Resolved for now. Filing SEV-2, assigning to eng-runtime and eng-ml for root cause and long-term mitigations.
Sam: Thx all :thumbsup:
